slot.brief: Match functional-group detection (Lassaigne's test: N, S, halogen) with correct observation/chemistry.

stem:
Match the element(s) detected in Lassaigne's test (List-I) with the characteristic species formed (List-II):

**List-I**
(P) Nitrogen only
(Q) Sulphur only
(R) Both Nitrogen and Sulphur
(S) Chlorine

**List-II**
(1) Violet complex, $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$
(2) Prussian blue, $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$
(3) Blood-red complex, $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$
(4) White precipitate, $\text{AgCl}$

verdicts.working: Lassaigne's test: N only gives sodium ferrocyanide → Prussian blue Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3 (P-2). S only gives Na2S → violet [Fe(CN)5NOS]4- with sodium nitroprusside (Q-1). Both N and S give NaSCN → blood-red [Fe(SCN)]2+ with Fe3+ (R-3). Cl gives AgCl white ppt soluble in NH4OH (S-4). Charges verified: nitroprusside-sulfide complex -4, FeSCN +2, Prussian blue neutral. Matches option (A).

working:
In Lassaigne's test:
1. Nitrogen alone forms sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), which on reaction with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and acidification with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives ferric ferrocyanide (Prussian blue), $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$. Thus, P $\to$ 2.
2. Sulphur alone forms sodium sulphide ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}$), which gives a violet colour with sodium nitroprusside due to the formation of $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$. Thus, Q $\to$ 1.
3. When both Nitrogen and Sulphur are present, sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) is formed, which reacts with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ to give a blood-red complex, $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$. Thus, R $\to$ 3.
4. Chlorine forms sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$), which gives a white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$ with acidified $\text{AgNO}_3$. Thus, S $\to$ 4.

Matching: P-(2), Q-(1), R-(3), S-(4).

Matches option (A).
